repo_notes.content: The reader is the app's owner, who is a beginner with no programming background, plus his partner. Write every page for that reader: plain language, short paragraphs, everyday comparisons, and a short explanation the first time any technical term appears (for example repository, branch, pull request, deploy, browser storage, database, authentication, security rules). Prefer tables, bullet lists and simple Mermaid diagrams over code. When code is shown, keep it short and explain what it does in one sentence.

What the project is: a moving planner web app for a couple moving from Minato-ku to Shibuya-ku in Tokyo (new lease starts 12/12/2026, move around 12/28, old lease ends 1/25/2027). It is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step. GitHub Pages publishes the main branch at https://shigenaru.github.io/move-planner/. Firebase (Google sign-in plus one Firestore document, plans/shared) stores the shared plan and syncs it live between the two phones; Firestore security rules allow only the couple's Google accounts. Each browser also keeps a copy in localStorage. The app is Japanese by default with an English toggle.

Important files: index.html (page shell and script loading), app.js (all screens, actions, date and phase logic, merge logic, drag to reorder, update check), data.js (the library of moving steps, note templates and holidays, in English), data.ja.js (Japanese text for the same steps and templates), sync.js (Google sign-in and Firestore live sync), firebase-config.js (public Firebase project settings), styles.css (look and layout), version.txt and bump-version.sh (version number that makes open apps reload after a deploy), docs/beginners-guide.md and docs/making-changes.md (beginner explanations). Use the docs folder as the main source for concept pages.

pages.title: Start Here
pages.purpose: A friendly overview: what the app does, who it is for, the four parts (app files, GitHub, GitHub Pages, Firebase) explained with everyday comparisons, and a map of the rest of the wiki.

pages.title: Key Concepts for Beginners
pages.purpose: A glossary-style page explaining repository, commit, branch, pull request, merge, deploy, public vs private repo, GitHub Pages, Firebase, Firestore, authentication, security rules, browser storage, and why the Firebase API key is not a password. Use simple analogies.

pages.title: How Your Data Is Saved and Synced
pages.purpose: Explain in plain language where the plan lives (each phone's browser storage and the Firebase cloud), what happens when you tick a step, how two people editing at once are merged item by item (newest change wins), the sign-in screen, signing out, and who can see what. Based on sync.js, the merge functions in app.js and docs/beginners-guide.md.

pages.title: How a Change Reaches Your Phone
pages.purpose: Walk through the software development life cycle for this project: idea, build on a branch, test, pull request, review and merge, GitHub Pages deploy, and the automatic reload driven by version.txt and bump-version.sh. Include how to review and merge a PR and how to undo a change. Based on docs/making-changes.md.

pages.title: Tour of the App's Features
pages.purpose: Describe each tab as a user would see it: Home, Steps (milestone phases, collapsing, adding steps, date ranges, memo previews), Calendar (key dates, overlap, multi-day bars), Notes and lists (templates, groups, drag to reorder, linking to steps), Budget (estimates, actual costs, flexible splits and settle-up), Info (addresses, contacts) and Settings (language, key dates, tailoring questions, live sync, backup).

pages.title: The Moving Steps Library
pages.purpose: Explain how the Japan-specific moving steps are defined in data.js and translated in data.ja.js: what each field means (title, why, how, where, what to bring, links), how suggested dates are calculated from the key dates, why city-office steps skip weekends and the 12/29-1/3 closure, how phases are chosen from a step's start date, and how to ask for a step to be added or changed.

pages.title: Code Tour for the Curious
pages.purpose: A gentle walkthrough of each file and what it is responsible for, in plain language, with at most a few very short code excerpts. Explain how the page is drawn from the saved data (render functions), how buttons trigger actions (data-act attributes), and how the language toggle works.

pages.title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
pages.purpose: Answer common questions: the app shows an old version (wait or reopen; version check), 'This Google account is not allowed', signing in on a new phone, adding another person's account to the Firebase rules, using the app offline, backups and restoring, costs, and what happens if Firebase or GitHub is down.
